claim.pdf_says:
1. Condition-1 is evaluated. ... 2. The current condition is evaluated.
        If the current condition is true:
            a. the induction variable associated with the current condition is set to its initialization value
            b. the condition to the left of the current condition becomes the current condition ...
        otherwise:
            a. if there is another AFTER phrase to the right of the current condition,
                —the condition associated with that AFTER phrase becomes the current condition
                —execution proceeds to the beginning of step b;
            b. otherwise
                —the specified set of statements is executed ...
claim.markdown_says:
1\. Condition-1 is evaluated.

   If condition-1 is true, ...

   2\. The current condition is evaluated.

   If the current condition is true:

   a. the induction variable associated with the current condition is set to its initialization value

   b. the condition to the left of the current condition becomes the current condition
...
   otherwise:

   a. if there is another AFTER phrase to the right of the current condition,

   —the condition associated with that AFTER phrase becomes the current condition

   —execution proceeds to the beginning of step b;

   b. otherwise

claim.why_it_matters: PERFORM general rule 9 e) is a four-level nested algorithm (numbered steps 1-2 under e), lettered a.-d. under 'If the current condition is true:' and a.-b. under 'otherwise:', em-dash actions under each). The transcription flattens every level to one indentation, so the two separate a./b. lists, the em-dash actions, and the e) parent are indistinguishable, and the cross-references 'step a' / 'step b' become ambiguous between the a)/b) rules, the 'true' a./b. and the 'otherwise' a./b. This is the normative execution order of PERFORM VARYING ... AFTER with TEST BEFORE.
claim.note: Wording is exact; only the list nesting is lost. Continues the flattening from p571-1 (rule 9 e) begins at the foot of page 571).

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 548 (PDF p572) and page-572.md agree word for word: steps 1 and 2, 'If the current condition is true:' a.-d., 'otherwise:' a.-b. with their em-dash actions, the NOTE, the 'During the execution...' paragraph and rule 10). The only difference is indentation depth: the markdown puts every item at 3 spaces where the PDF nests them. Every list marker (1., 2., a.-d., a.-b., em dashes) and every lead-in line ('If the current condition is true:', 'otherwise:') is kept in its original order, so the nesting can be recovered from the text alone. The 'step a'/'step b' cross-references read the same as in the PDF, and the markdown adds no ambiguity the printed wording does not already carry. No text is missing, moved or changed. Flattened indentation is formatting, which the verification criteria exclude.
